subject: Exception request: packaging credit & discount for Orbital Health - pilot
body:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orbitalhealth.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging + pricing for Enterprise pilot - Redwood

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team loved the throughput and observability pieces. We are ready to move forward with a pilot (50 concurrent users, 6 months) but procurement pushed back on list pricing. They are asking for a significant credit on packaging and a steeper first-year discount to fit within our Q2 budget envelope.

Key asks from procurement:
- 40% discount off list for year 1 (they called this a necessary concession to make budget)
- Waive packaging fees for the pilot (two months free of packaging/ingress fees)
- SOC2 evidence + standard security questionnaire completed before PO

Budget note: if we can get close on pricing, they will sign an ARR-backed 12-month enterprise contract after pilot. Expected initial committed ARR is ~$240k for year 1.

Can you update the quote and let me know what is possible? Procurement asked to see an updated quote and an approval memo if this requires leadership sign-off.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of AI Platforms — Orbital Health
Tom.Reynolds@orbitalhealth.ai

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orbitalhealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:03:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging + pricing for Enterprise pilot - Redwood

Tom — appreciate the clarity. Short answer: we can make a concession, but 40% is outside my delegated discount band. I ran a quick counter and attached an updated quote and our MOP for pilot scope.

Proposed response for procurement:
- Year 1: 25% off list on inference usage (applies to token charges and embeddings)
- Packaging credit: waive first two months of packaging fees for the pilot (covers ingress and storage)
- Conditions: 12-month committed contract to follow pilot; Redwood to be listed as a reference customer; standard SLOs in contract

Why 25% vs 40%: preserves unit economics for our serving footprint and keeps margin to cover dedicated capacity we may need during pilot spikes.

I've attached: redwood_quote_2026-02-26.xlsx (proposed numbers) and Orbital_AMP_MOP_v3.pdf (pilot milestones, security checkpoints).

If procurement pushes for >30% we will need VP/CFO approval. Karthik — looping you in for deal context and recommendation.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_quote_2026-02-26.xlsx (spreadsheet), Orbital_AMP_MOP_v3.pdf (PDF)

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orbitalhealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:18:42 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging + pricing for Enterprise pilot - Redwood

Diego / Tom — quick context from AE side:
- Competitive pressure: Orbital is evaluating two vendors; one is offering a deeper promotional discount to secure the pilot.
- Upside: if pilot succeeds, they convert to ~ $240k ARR committed for year 1 and expansion potential into 2027.
- Risk: heavy bursty usage in the pilot will increase our serving cost; packaging credit helps but we need to ensure caching and batching controls are enabled.

My recommended approval path:
1) Approve up to 30% off for year 1 (conditional).
2) Offer packaging credit = 2 months waived (as Diego proposed).
3) Require a 12-month committed contract to be signed within 30 days of pilot completion; include published performance KPIs and a reference clause.
4) Add a 6-month runway to migrate to standard pricing in year 2 (step down pricing).

Financial impact (approx):
- If we approve 30% year 1 discount, expected realized ARR = $168k (year 1), incremental service cost ~ $36k; trade-off acceptable given reference and expansion.

If leadership will greenlight 30% + packaging credit I can take the final quote to procurement and move to DocuSign.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orbitalhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Exception memo: request VP/CFO sign-off — Orbital Health (DW-2026-ORB-2345)

Laura / Marissa — I need VP/CFO sign-off for an exception to our standard discount cap for a strategic pilot with Orbital Health. Summary below and attached supporting docs.

Summary of ask:
- Approve a 30% discount off list for year 1 (redwood_quote_2026-02-26.xlsx)
- Approve packaging credit: waive packaging fees for first 2 months of the 6-month pilot (Orbital_AMP_MOP_v3.pdf)
- Conditions: 12-month committed contract to be signed after successful pilot, Redwood listed as reference, standard SLOs applied

Business case / rationale:
- Conversion likelihood: High (internal procurement signals + clinical partner endorsement)
- Expected committed ARR (post-pilot): ~$240k; year 1 realized ARR at 30% discount = ~$168k
- Strategic value: high potential for case study in clinical AI vertical and acceleration into two other Orbital business lines (estimated expansion > 2x in 2027)
- Competitive dynamics: alternative vendor is offering deeper upfront incentives; matching more of the ask increases win probability without additional long-term concessions

Financial considerations:
- Estimated incremental cost to Redwood for pilot (bandwidth, compute bursts, support): ~$36k
- Net margin impact for year 1 at 30% discount: acceptable given reference and expansion potential

Recommendation (ask):
- Approve the 30% year-1 discount and 2-month packaging credit for the pilot. If approved I will:
  - Update quote and push to DocuSign (link: https://www.docusign.com/EnvelopeID/ABC-2345)
  - Confirm SOC2 evidence packet delivery within 5 business days
  - Add explicit step-down pricing for year 2 in the contract

Please reply to this thread with "APPROVED" or "NOT APPROVED" and any suggested edits. If you prefer, Marissa, I can route a short memo to Finance with the P&L impact broken down.

Attachments: redwood_quote_2026-02-26.xlsx, Orbital_AMP_MOP_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0182

--
Diego Fernandez
